section.sectionSummaryBrief: The commandments are called a covenant because they contain two aspects: physical objects and the Supernal Will, which are unified.
section.t: And likewise, the commandments are called a covenant,
because in the commandments there are also two aspects,
for they themselves are made from physical things,
and in them is the drawing down of the Supernal Will,
for Will is above wisdom.
And these two aspects in the commandments are not two separate matters,
but rather they are one matter,
for the commandments that are clothed in physical things,
they themselves are the Supernal Will,
for thus it arose in His Will to fulfill the commandments specifically in physicality.
And because He is the Will of the Blessed One that is above even wisdom,
therefore it descends below specifically into physical things.
However, this very thing—that through Torah and commandments it will be possible for the unification of the souls of Israel with Ein Sof—
for seemingly,
since Ein Sof is not at all from any of these attributes,
how can the action of lower beings take hold so that there will be a face-to-face unification,
since He is not at all from any of these attributes,
it is impossible for there to be a face-to-face unification,
whether from the side of Ein Sof or from the side of the souls of Israel—
concerning this it is said, "I stand between Hashem and you to tell you the word of Hashem,"
for "I am who I am" is the aspect of Keter that is above both of them,
and through the power of Keter, unification is effected through the Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The verse "And it will be, because you will listen" refers to gathering the scattered sparks of the soul and the laws of Torah, which enables unification.
section.t: And this is, "And it will be, because you will listen to these judgments,"
for behold,
the translation of "judgment" is "halacha,"
which is the matter of the laws of the Torah,
and this means that since this verse explains the unification of the souls of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, as above,
therefore it says "these judgments,"
for the unification is through the laws of the Torah.
And "you will listen" is an expression of gathering,
like "And Shaul gathered," etc.,
and the matter is to gather and collect all the scattered sparks of his Divine soul that became bound to foreign desires,
through the multitude of thoughts and the scattering of the soul,
for although it is written,
"And Hashem your God will bless you in all that you do" specifically,
that the action must be in physicality,
nevertheless,
the thought need not be immersed in this,
and as it is written,
"When you eat the labor of your hands,"
that it should be only the labor of the hands,
but not the labor of the mind and heart,
therefore one must gather the sparks that were scattered through the scattering of the soul,
and as it is written,
"If your dispersed will be at the ends of the heavens, from there He will gather you."
And just as one must gather the scattered sparks of his soul,
so too must there be gathering in the laws of the Torah,
for from the scattering that occurred in his soul,
there is caused for him concealment and hiding also in the Torah,
so that he cannot clarify and rule on the law in its truth,
and concerning this it says, "you will listen to the judgments,"
these are the laws,
for "you will listen" is gathering,
that there must be gathering in his soul and gathering in the laws of the Torah.
And this is also what is written,
"And you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
for the souls of Israel are called by the name "your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
and they are three divisions of levels in the souls of Israel,
Kohanim, Leviim, and Yisraelim.
"Your grain" refers to Yisraelim,
for just as in physicality, bread is the main thing,
for "bread sustains the heart of man,"
and the other foods are only additions to the bread,
so too in the souls of Israel, the main thing is Yisraelim,
for even Kohanim and Leviim are Yisraelim,
except that they have an additional advantage of Kohanim and Leviim,
therefore Yisraelim are called "your grain."
"Your wine" refers to Leviim,
for the service of the Leviim is in saying song,
and song is only said over wine.
"And your oil" refers to Kohanim,
for their service is in the aspect of oil,
in quietness and with a willing heart.
And this is, "And you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
which is the matter of gathering the scattered sparks in all three types of the souls of Israel.
Also, the interpretation of "And you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil" is the matter of the gathering that must be in the Torah,
for the Torah is also called by the name "your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
and they are the divisions of levels that exist in the Torah.
"Your grain" is the revealed part of the Torah,
"your wine" is the inner dimension of the Torah,
the secrets of the Torah,
and "your oil" is the secrets of secrets,
like oil that floats on top of wine,
as explained in Imrei Binah
at length.
And this is, "And you will gather your grain, etc.,"
which is the matter of the gathering that must be in all parts of the Torah.
And this is, "And it will be, because you will listen to these judgments,"
that when there is the gathering of the scattered sparks of his soul and the gathering in the Torah,
and in general it is the service of "you will listen," "and you will guard," and "and you will do," which are from below upward,
through this there will also be drawn down from above downward,
so that there will be a face-to-face unification of the souls of Israel and Ein Sof, blessed be He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In the service stemming from the Supernal Will, above reason, there is no need for gathering, and the Torah draws down the light from above the chain of descent.
section.t: However, all this is in the service from below upward as it is from the side of the lower will born of intellect.
But in the service as it is from the side of the Supernal Will,
that is, the service of the will of the heart that is above reason and knowledge,
which in general is the love of "with all your might" stated in the first paragraph of the Shema,
behold, in this paragraph the verse "And you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil" is not mentioned
(which is done from the matter of "if your dispersed will be," etc.)
as in the second paragraph of the Shema,
because from the side of the love of "with all your might,"
which is the matter of doing the will of the Place,
as mentioned above
in the name of the Maggid, that it is the matter of drawing down the Will of the Blessed One that is above the chain of descent,
behold, from the side of drawing down this aspect, there is no need for the service of gathering,
for rather, as it is written,
"And He will bless, etc., your grain, your wine, and your oil,"
so that there will not be in them the aspect of scattering of the soul to foreign desires, etc.,
for this matter applies specifically in the chain of descent,
but from the side of the love of "with all your might" that draws down the will that is above the chain of descent,
this matter does not apply.
And this is the true matter of the covenant of Torah,
for the matter of Torah is a drawing down from above to below,
that is, the drawing down of the Supernal light as it is
(not according to the measure of the created beings),
and it is the light that is above the chain of descent,
for prayer is an elevation from below to above,
"And you will gather your grain, etc.,"
but the Torah is a drawing down from above to below,
the drawing down of the light that is above the chain of descent,
and this is through the prior service of the will of the heart,
the aspect of "with all your might,"
for then through the Torah is drawn down the light that is above the chain of descent,
and this is the true matter of the covenant of Torah,
that the Torah connects and unifies the souls of Israel with the aspect that is above the chain of descent.
